title: What the Carried-Forward Share Is Measured On at a Period End
content:
On a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card, the share that carries forward out of a closing benefit period is not always measured on the same quantity. What it is measured on turns on whether an allowance was loaded for the period at all, and on how much of it the member spent.

**The rule.** The base the carried-forward share is measured on is the whole allowance loaded for the period, where an allowance was loaded for it and the member spent at least half of that allowance from the card in it; it is what is left unspent from that period, where an allowance was loaded for it and the member spent less than half of that allowance from the card in it; and nothing carries forward in every other case.

**How the half is judged.** What the member spent from the card in the period, for this comparison, is the total of the transactions that settled in it. That total is set against half of the allowance loaded for the period. A member who spent exactly half of it falls on the first row, the comparison being made at not less than half.

| What the closing period shows | The base the share is measured on |
|---|---|
| an allowance was loaded for the period, and the settled transactions come to at least half of it | the whole allowance loaded for the period |
| an allowance was loaded for the period, and the settled transactions come to less than half of it | what is left unspent from that period |
| no allowance was loaded for the period | nothing carries forward |

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** A period carrying an allowance of 135.00 USD on which 70.00 USD settled: the settled total is at least half of 135.00 USD, so the base is the whole 135.00 USD. On the same period with 60.00 USD settled, the settled total is less than half, so the base is what is left unspent from the period. At exactly 67.50 USD settled the first row is reached, and the base is the whole 135.00 USD.
